item.title: Set Up a GPS NTP Server with chrony for Your Homelab
item.description:
Intro

I wanted to easily synchronize the time between my VMs and decided to set up an ntp server to accomplish this. Since a USB GPS device is relatively inexpensive, I thought it would be a great addition to the project.

For the following examples, I used aptitude and vim.

How to Set Up Chrony with gpsd

Setting up chrony with a GPS turns your host into a stratum 1 NTP server. The USB GPS locks onto satellite time, gpsd reads it from the serial device, and chrony uses it as a reference clock and serves it to the rest of the LAN. My VMs sync to that host instead of reaching out to public NTP servers. This matters for identity, as services relying on Kerberos reject logins when a host’s clock drifts more than 5 minutes from the domain controller.
